title: How to Make Your Apartment Look Expensive on a Budget
h1: How to Make Your Apartment Look Expensive: Designer Moves That Work in Any Rental
description: Learn how to make your apartment look expensive with designer moves for curtains, lighting, rugs, art and hardware, plus a budget guide for renters.
keyword: how to make your apartment look expensive
secondary_keywords: how to make an apartment look luxurious
cheap ways to make your home look expensive
excerpt: Curtains hung high, warm layered light, bigger rugs and fewer, better objects: the designer moves that make any apartment look luxurious without a big budget.
image_alt: Neutral sofa styled with linen and velvet pillows, showing how to make your apartment look expensive with layered textures
key_takeaways: Declutter and edit first: clear surfaces and grouped decor make a room look expensive for free.
Hang curtain rods 4–6 in. above the window frame (or higher), 8–12 in. wider on each side, with floor-length panels.
Use warm 2700K bulbs with a CRI of 90+ and light every room from at least three sources.
Size up: an 8 x 10 ft rug in most living rooms and art about two-thirds the width of the furniture below it.
Spend on curtains, rugs and lighting; save on decor accessories, hardware and art prints.

faq.q: How can I make my apartment look expensive on a budget?
faq.a: Start with free changes: declutter surfaces, pull furniture off the walls and group decor in odd numbers. Then put your money into the items with the biggest visual impact, namely floor-length curtains hung high and wide, warm high-CRI light bulbs, a properly sized rug and one large piece of framed art. Save on accessories and buy solid materials secondhand.

faq.q: What makes a room look cheap?
faq.a: The most common culprits are clutter, rugs that are too small, curtains that stop short of the floor, art hung too high, matching furniture sets, visible cords, shiny synthetic fabrics and cool, harsh overhead lighting. Fixing even three or four of these makes a noticeable difference in how expensive a room looks.

faq.q: What colors make an apartment look luxurious?
faq.a: Warm neutrals such as ivory, oatmeal, greige, taupe and camel, paired with black accents and natural wood, are the easiest route to a luxurious look. Deep tonal colors like olive, navy, burgundy and chocolate also read as high-end. Keep the palette tight, with three or four related shades repeated in a roughly 60-30-10 split.

faq.q: How high should curtains be hung to make a room look bigger?
faq.a: Mount the rod at least 4 to 6 inches above the window frame, or about halfway between the frame and the ceiling, and go higher if your windows are short. Extend the rod 8 to 12 inches past the frame on each side and use panels long enough to just touch the floor. This makes windows look larger and ceilings taller.

faq.q: Can renters make an apartment look luxurious without damaging it?
faq.a: Yes. Most of the biggest upgrades are reversible: curtains, rugs, lamps, plug-in sconces, bulbs, pillows, art, mirrors and swapped cabinet hardware or showerheads that you store and reinstall before moving out. Check your lease and ask your landlord before changing fixtures, painting or drilling into walls.
